_comment: Single source of truth for how the XCUITest suites are tiered and sharded.
component  focused: one test drives one feature and asserts on it.
smoke      broad: one test walks a path that joins several features

soak       leak probes, run through tool/run_leak_harness.sh (harness: true).
             The tests themselves only assert the screen appeared — the actual
             leak check is a pixel scan of frames captured by the harness's mock
             upload server, so running them WITHOUT the harness proves nothing.
             A harness shard must hold exactly one test; the plan job enforces it.
             Formerly described as cheap enough to gate a
             PR once split one-test-per-shard, so they ride under the slowest
             smoke shard rather than extending it.
Shards run as parallel jobs against one shared build, so wall-clock is the
SLOWEST shard, not the sum. `seconds` is the measured runtime of the tests
in that shard (GitHub macos-15, run 33612331880) and exists so the packing
can be rebalanced from data rather than guesswork. Keep shards under ~200s.
Adding a UI test? Add it to a shard here or it will not run in CI.
The tier-coverage check in ci-ui-tests.yml fails the build if a test method
exists in the source but is missing from this file.
